top.title: Breaking: Court sacks Mark-led ADC Exco, voids Atiku’s candidacy
top.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja The Federal High Court in Abuja has sacked the Senator David Mark-led executives of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and invalidated all actions they took on behalf of the party. The actions included the nomination of a former vice president, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, as the party’s presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections. Atiku, whose name was earlier published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) as a candidate for the presidential poll, has since chosen a former governor of Rivers State, Rotimi Amaechi, as his running mate. However, in a judgment delivered on Thursday by Justice Peter Lifu, the court declared illegal the Senator Mark-led Caretaker Committee of the ADC, which organised the primary election that produced Atiku as the party’s presidential flag bearer. The court found merit in a suit brought before it by the aggrieved former National Deputy Chairman (North-East) of the party, Nafiu Bala Gombe. Gombe had approached the court to query the process through which the Senator Mark-led Committee took over the reins of leadership of the party. He maintained that, with the resignation of the former National Chairman, Chief Ralph Nwosu, he (Gombe) was qualified to assume the party’s leadership. Consequently, he, among other things, prayed the court to nullify all actions taken on behalf of the party by the Senator Mark-led leadership. Listed as defendants in the suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, were the ADC, INEC, Senator Mark, Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola and Chief Ralph Nwosu. The plaintiff further urged the court to restrain Senator Mark and Aregbesola from parading themselves as National Chairman and Secretary, respectively, of the ADC, insisting that their emergence violated the party’s constitution and the provisions of the Electoral Act. The court upheld the plaintiff’s claim and granted his reliefs, a verdict that could spark a chain of reactions in the polity, with the presidential election scheduled for January 16, 2027. Already, the ADC has vowed to appeal the judgment. Reacting to the outcome of the case, the National Welfare Secretary of the ADC, Mr. Nkemakolam Ukandu, who was later joined as an interested party in the matter, said the verdict would be challenged at the appellate court. The development comes barely 24 hours after the party’s candidate, Atiku, held a massive rally in Sokoto State as part of his campaign for the 2027 presidential election. top.title: Former F1 champion Jones dies aged 80
top.description: Jones helped turn Williams into one of the major forces in F1 [Getty Images] Alan Jones, the last Australian and first Williams driver to win the Formula 1 world title, has died at the age of 80. Jones raced in F1 between 1975 and 1986, winning the title in 1980 to become the first of Williams' seven world champions. Jones, who turned 80 on Monday, won 12 grands prix in his career and raced competitively in other formats until 2002. "We are extremely saddened to announce the passing of our beloved Alan, who passed away on 5 November following a short illness," his wife Amanda Butler-Davis said in a statement released on her behalf by Motorsport Australia. "He will be dearly missed and fondly remembered by those closest to him, as well as the many fans whose support he was always grateful for." Jones started the first of his 116 F1 races in a Hesketh at the 1975 Spanish Grand Prix. He won his first race for the Shadow team in Austria in 1977 before joining Williams the following year. After finishing third in the drivers' championship in 1979, he won five races in 1980 and finished on the podium in all but one of the grands prix he completed, taking the title ahead of Nelson Piquet. Jones was the second Australian to win the F1 championship, after Jack Brabham in 1959, 1960 and 1966. Jones remains the most recent Australian to triumph at the Australian Grand Prix, winning at Melbourne's Calder Park Raceway in 1980 when the race was not part of the world championship. He finished third in the drivers' standings in 1981, winning in Las Vegas for what proved to be his final race victory. He retired at the end of the season. Having appeared in one race for Arrows in 1983, Jones made a full-time comeback with new team Haas in 1985 and raced largely unsuccessfully the following year. He continued to compete in touring car and endurance races, mostly in Australia, and became a popular motorsports pundit on television in his home country. "Alan dedicated his life to motorsport, building a legacy that will live on through the countless people he touched along the way," Butler-Davis said. "Through his achievements, passion and unmistakable character, both on and off the track, Alan left an enduring mark on the sport both nationally and across the globe." Breaking new ground with Williams Jones, the Williams FW07 and Patrick Head and Frank Williams in Brazil in 1981 [Getty Images] Alan Jones' time at the very peak of F1 was short - essentially just under three years from mid-1979 to the end of 1981 - but he left a lasting impression. Jones is synonymous with the Williams team, having become their first world champion in 1980, and he formed a close, almost brotherly bond with co-founders Frank Williams and Patrick Head. Williams and Head loved Jones' pugnacious, no-nonsense approach, and between them they were the leading force in F1 for a short time, as the team first emerged at the forefront of the sport. top.title: One year after 'Let it Rip' meeting, Trevor Lawrence has elevated game
top.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars were a surprising 4-3, but his quarterback was still searching to sync his in-week preparation and game-day production when Liam Coen welcomed Trevor Lawrence into his second-floor office on Oct. 20, 2025. Lawrence was a tireless worker who made the right pre-snap decisions but was plagued by bouts of indecisiveness. Before sending him on his bye week, Coen showed Lawrence multiple examples in which the play was right there had he pulled the trigger. “I just have to trust it,” Lawrence told Coen. The summit could eventually be remembered as one of the most important meetings — The "Let It Rip" meeting — in Jaguars history. The coach showed confidence and belief in his franchise quarterback but also urged him to be more aggressive. In the 17 regular season games since, the Jaguars are 14-3 and Lawrence has totals of 37 touchdowns, 11 interceptions, 4,669 passing yards, a 63.9 completion rate and a 109.9 passer rating. High-level stuff. MVP stuff. Winning stuff. A player who used to tease with bits of elite play is now one of the NFL’s best quarterbacks. He enters the Jaguars’ Nov. 5 game at the Baltimore Ravens with a league-best 112.6 passer rating; he started the season with a career 86.3 rating. The Jaguars are 5-2 thanks in part to Lawrence’s level-jump — check that, multi-level jump. Just as the Chicago Bears have been reborn with the Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams, so have the Jaguars with Coen and Lawrence. Admit it: For the first time since maybe 1999, you, the Jaguars fan, expects your team to win every week and when they don’t, there is a sky-is-falling reaction. Feels good, doesn’t it? It sure does within Jaguars headquarters, where the collaboration between Coen and Lawrence has advanced to the pro football equivalent of Ph.D. courses. “Very far,” Coen told The Times-Union on Oct. 20 of Lawrence's progress. “I’m very, very pleased with how he’s seeing things.” What is it like to be around Coen and Lawrence in the quarterback meeting room, when class is in session and plays are tossed out, added or revised? top.title: Jeremiah Smith is 164 yards from another Big Ten record
top.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 31: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes in action against the USC Trojans during the second quarter at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on October 31, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images Lost in the frustration of Ohio State’s 30-18 loss at USC was another piece of history from Jeremiah Smith. With just over two minutes left, Luke Fahey found him for a one yard touchdown. It was the 40th touchdown catch of Smith’s career, breaking Braylon Edwards’ Big Ten record of 39, which had stood since 2004. It didn’t feel like much of a celebration in the moment, but it’s worth remembering just how fast Smith is rewriting the record books. Smith already owns every major receiving record at Ohio State, and now he holds the Big Ten’s career touchdown mark too. The next record could fall this Saturday. The yardage record is within reach Smith caught 10 passes for 83 yards at USC, giving him 3,625 career receiving yards. The Big Ten record belongs to Purdue’s John Standeford, who finished with 3,788 yards from 2000 to 2003. That puts Smith 163 yards from tying the record and 164 from breaking it. That’s a big number for most receivers. For Smith, it’s an ordinary afternoon. He had 151 yards against Ball State, 164 at Texas, 217 against Illinois and 206 at Iowa. He’s averaging over 130 receiving yards per game this season, with 62 catches for 1,067 yards and 13 touchdowns through eight games. When I wrote about the Big Ten record chase in early October, I predicted JJ would break this one at USC on Halloween. Sayin’s injury, a quiet day at Indiana and USC’s game plan pushed it back a week. The timing might work out even better. Breaking it at home against Oregon, in front of the Ohio Stadium crowd, would be a pretty fitting way to do it. Can he get there with Fahey? That’s the real question. Smith’s production has dipped over the last two games. Against Indiana, he had a season-low 68 yards against a defense that threw extra bodies at him on almost every snap. At USC, with Fahey making his first start, he caught 10 passes but averaged just 8.3 yards per catch as Ohio State leaned on quick, short throws. That makes sense. Fahey needed easy completions, and Smith is the most reliable target on the field. But it also means the big plays haven’t been there. To get 164 yards against Oregon, Smith will probably need at least one or two explosive plays down the field. I think there’s reason to believe those will come. Fahey now has a full game under his belt and another week of practice as the starter. Smith said after Indiana that it would, “take time” to build the same chemistry with a new quarterback, but he’s already Fahey’s top target. Smith also caught the record breaking touchdown at USC, which tells you Fahey is looking for him when it matters most. The more reps those two get together, the more comfortable Fahey should be giving Smith a chance to make a play down the field.

top.title: Marco Rose embraces Premier League life and jokes about Thomas Tuchel
top.description: Marco Rose embraces Premier League life and jokes about Thomas Tuchel Former Bundesliga coach Marco Rose has spoken enthusiastically about his first months in English football. The 50-year-old, who previously coached Borussia Mönchengladbach, Borussia Dortmund, and RB Leipzig, is currently enjoying an upturn in fortunes with AFC Bournemouth following a difficult start to the Premier League campaign. After failing to win any of their opening six league fixtures, Bournemouth have recently registered three consecutive victories. Rose’s side have also enjoyed success in European competition, with the German trainer preparing for Thursday’s Europa League encounter against Sparta Prague. Speaking in an interview with Kicker , Rose reflected on his experience in the Premier League and the differences between German and English football. “It’s something special to be able to work there,” Rose explained. “One senses the global attention. It’s football in its purest form. I appreciate German fan culture, but I also like the English version. It’s a little quieter here at times, but when the match calls for it, the stadiums generate extraordinary energy. I like the people in England, who treat one another with great respect. I really feel comfortable here.” Marco Rose jokes about Thomas Tuchel and Marcus Tavernier Rose also reserved praise for Bournemouth attacker Marcus Tavernier, who has scored five goals in nine Premier League appearances this season. Asked whether the 26-year-old might soon receive a call-up from England national team coach Thomas Tuchel, Rose declined to speculate but acknowledged his player’s impressive performances. “You’ll have to ask Thomas about that,” Rose remarked. “But I think several of our lads have made a good case for themselves, and Marcus in particular gives us a great deal.” When asked whether Tuchel had attended a Bournemouth home fixture to watch Tavernier, Rose delivered a lighthearted response. “No, I don’t think so,” Rose said with a laugh. “Perhaps he couldn’t get a ticket because our stadium is a little smaller.” GGFN | Peter Weis

top.title: Three Important Questions for Dodgers Before 2027
top.description: Oct 3, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers starting pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) looks on from the mound after giving up a solo home run to Atlanta Braves catcher Sean Murphy (12) in game one of the NLDS of the 2026 MLB … | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor Last season ended in disappointment for the Los Angeles Dodgers. Now, they must assess themselves as they prepare for the future. Here are three questions they must ask if they want to continue their prolonged success into 2027 and beyond. In the Market for Pitching Again? Los Angeles knows better than most that one can never have enough pitching. To that end, they traded for Tarik Skubal at the trade deadline this year. Now, are they willing to keep him? The left-hander is expected to earn a pretty penny this year. Moreover, he has Scott Boras as his agent and an abbreviated window with which to negotiate as December 1 approaches. Los Angeles and President of Baseball Operations Andrew Friedman have plenty of money at their disposal, provided that their owner doesn’t sell the team. Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) pitches during the first inning of their National League Championship Series game against the Milwaukee Brewers at American Family Field on Oct 11, 2026. However, Los Angeles, with a few notable exceptions, is very hesitant to dole out long-term contracts to a player entering free agency who is entering his third decade. The more likely option for a mutual agreement would be a shorter deal in length with a higher AAV, similar to the Kyle Tucker deal. It is said that Los Angeles has some competition for the left-hander’s services; the New York Mets and Chicago Cubs are also interested. Skubal did seem to like it in Los Angeles, but it’s still a question where he will end up. However, those in the know expect a deal signed by December 1. The Youth Movement? Los Angeles has the oldest roster in baseball, and it showed during the National League Championship Series against the World Champion Milwaukee Brewers. The question is how young will the Dodgers go without compromising the veteran core? There is no question that there will be some turnover on the margins. Enrique and Teoscar Hernandez will probably be on different teams in 2027. Josue DePaula will probably cement his place on the roster. Do they sign or trade for a shortstop like Elly de La Cruz ? Will they move Mookie Betts to second base to preserve him from wear and tear on his body? Friedman, in his year-end press conference, addressed the age of the players, but he didn’t seem overly concerned right now. He pointed out that whoever they place on the roster must be major-league ready and fit the team’s needs. It will be interesting to see the evolution of the roster as the offseason progresses. nigeria.title: Netanyahu loses religious party’s support as rival tipped to form government
nigeria.description: An ultra-Orthodox Jewish party long aligned with Benjamin Netanyahu declined on Thursday to recommend him to stay as Israel’s prime minister, as signs grew that rival Gadi Eisenkot will have the first chance to form a government. President Isaac Herzog was holding a second day of consultations with political parties after the October 27 election, in which neither Netanyahu — a polarising right-winger who has led Israel through three years of war — nor Eisenkot secured enough votes for a majority. United Torah Judaism, which backed Netanyahu after the previous five elections, in its meeting with Herzog declined to recommend Netanyahu again as prime minister, although it also did not side with Eisenkot. The party informed Herzog “that it has decided not to recommend any member of Knesset to form a government,” the president’s office said in a statement, referring to the 120-member parliament in which United Torah Judaism has won seven seats. The party, which represents ultra-Orthodox Jews of Ashkenazi origin, who mostly hail from or have roots in Europe, as well as Shas, which represents the same community but of Sephardic, or mostly Middle Eastern and North African descent, have both been backed by Netanyahu as they push to maintain the exemption from military service for religious students. Netanyahu has preserved the exemption but stopped short of enshrining it in law, in the face of major resentment from many other Israelis as reservists serve multiple tours due to the wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. “In whatever government is next formed, our immediate item is sorting out the status of Torah students,” United Torah Judaism lawmaker Isaac Pindrus said. Eisenkot, a former military chief seeking to unite the centre and centre-right, has been adamant about closing exemptions to military service, with some of his opposition allies harshly criticising the ultra-Orthodox as self-serving. Observers say United Torah Judaism’s approach may be aimed more at punishing Netanyahu and showing that their votes cannot be taken for granted, while they could still serve in a government if he were to form one. Herzog will meet representatives of the major parties later on Thursday before tasking one lawmaker with forming a government. He generally bases his decision on which person receives the most party recommendations, making it likely he will ask Eisenkot. Once Herzog gives the mandate, that lawmaker will have 28 days to form a government, with a potential 14-day extension. If the lawmaker fails, Herzog will then task someone else. Netanyahu’s bloc — including United Torah Judaism — has 53 seats in the new parliament, as opposed to 48 for Eisenkot’s bloc. Israeli-Arab parties soared in strength on the back of anger over Netanyahu’s hard-right government, winning 19 seats. Speaking during his ongoing media chat in Portharcourt, Rivers State, on Thursday, Wike dismissed his involvement in the court judgement, stating that those linking his name are only being mischievous Though he admitted publicly disagreeing with the Governor of Imo, Hope Uzodinma, over his rainbow coalition initiative, he denied being in the know of ongoing internal political issues in the APC. Further speaking on his rainbow coalition initiative, Wike posed a question to the Imo State Governor, asking, “What is Uzodimma afraid of?” “I didn’t go to court; I’m not from APC. People are saying that because a day before that judgement he had openly warned his people there’s no Rainbow Coalition; if I see you I’ll collect the vehicle. So when the judgement came, they said it was me. How could it have been me? What is Hope Uzodinma afraid of in the Rainbow Coalition?” He said both priorities should be working to see the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in 2027, adding that if there is an initiative to achieve that, “What then is the issue?” he asked. “Your business is to make sure Mr President wins elections. At the national assembly level, so many factors come in, including zoning. I owe no apologies that Rochas is my friend; after all, he has friends in Rivers State that are my political enemies; will I go and kill them? No!!” “If he’s a strong man, he shouldn’t be afraid. You’re strong; whatever you see you take!” The post APC Imo-West Senatorial Ticket: Wike Denies Link To Court Judgement appeared first on Channels Television .

nigeria.title: Growing Debt Burden By Tinubu Will Be Passed To Future Generation — NDC
nigeria.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has called on Nigerians to turn out in massive numbers in the 2027 elections and use their votes to demand accountability, fiscal responsibility, and a government that puts the people’s interests first, according to a statement by the party’s National Presidential Campaign Council Spokesperson, Dr. Chiogo Constance Ikokwu. The party said the country’s growing debt burden, in light of new loan requests by President Bola Tinubu, and the obligations being passed on to future generations, make the 2027 general election too important for citizens to sit out. The Party’s plea followed President Tinubu again, asking the National Assembly to approve a new external borrowing plan of $7.7 billion (approximately ₦10.79 trillion) to help finance the 2026 budget deficit. “…making this a case of one week, new loan”, the statement said partly. Ikokwu noted that the party’s passionate appeal to Nigerians is to turn out massively and vote for Peter Obi and Engr. Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso on January 16, 2027, just as Americans demonstrated the power of the ballot in their November 4, 2026 elections. NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, says he will serve for only one term of four years if elected President in 2027. She observed that Americans, like Nigerians, are grappling with the high cost of living and economic hardship. Rather than merely grumbling or resigning themselves to their circumstances, she said, Americans turned out to exercise their democratic rights, demonstrating that the power to change government ultimately rests with the electorate. Dr Ikokwu therefore urged Nigerians to emulate Americans, whom she described as champions of democratic participation, by coming out in their millions to vote for Obi and Kwankwaso. Dr Ikokwu said: “Truly, it seems that right now, we cannot stop President Tinubu from his One Week! New Loan! One Week! New Loan! borrowing spree, which is already hitting the roof, because, regrettably, he has pocketed the National Assembly. We seem to have a rubber-stamp legislature that, before a loan request formally gets to its desk, it has already been endorsed. “But Nigerians should not despair. The ballot remains our most powerful instrument of change. We appeal to citizens to use their votes to rescue the country from this debt trap and entrust its future to a government committed to transparency, accountability and prudent management of public resources.” The NDC reiterated that the country’s economic future must not be mortgaged by unsustainable borrowing and the mismanagement of public resources. nigeria.title: Race for 2028 heats up after US midterms firestorm
nigeria.description: President Donald Trump’s stunning midterms defeat by the Democrats has upended another US election — the race to replace him in the White House in 2028. The crushing defeat for the Republicans is particularly stinging for Vice President JD Vance, who had been the frontrunner but now risks being seen as tied to his lame-duck boss. But the midterms are a potential launchpad for rising Democratic stars like Georgia senator Jon Ossoff, whose youthful vibe has already drawn comparisons to former president Barack Obama. – Republicans in turmoil – The MAGA coalition that shot Trump to power in 2016 and 2024 effectively collapsed in Tuesday’s midterms, leaving any presumptive Republican heir with a mountain to climb. Long seen as the odds-on favorite for the Republican nomination in 2028, Vance is the most obvious victim after hitching his wagon to Trump throughout the midterms campaigns with rallies in swing states. The ambitious 42-year-old quickly tried to distance himself from the electoral disaster, blaming it on Trump’s unpopular war on Iran in a long thesis posted on X on Wednesday. But voters are likely to reject his attempts to disown Trump. It’s a familiar problem for US vice presidents. Former Democratic candidate and vice president Kamala Harris suffered from a similar problem in 2024 when she said that “there’s not a thing that comes to mind” when asked how she’d differentiate herself from Joe Biden. “The bad news for Vance is that sitting vice presidents seldom win the presidency,” James Lindsay of the Council for Foreign Relations, said. Trump’s Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s name has also been bandied about. Rubio, 55, has kept a far lower profile during the midterms but any top official in Trump’s administration will struggle to wash their hands of the Iran war. The Republicans’ midterm disaster could, however, be a boost for other possible candidates. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, 48, who ran against Trump for the Republican nomination in 2024, has suddenly become very vocal. He described the Democratic sweep as “the political equivalent of a meteor strike” — and pointed out that it was only in his own state that Republicans held them off. Texas Senator Ted Cruz, 55, has also left the door open, having run against Trump in 2016 — although his chances may have been harmed by the Democrats’ stunning senate and governor wins in the midterms in his state. – Democrats on a high – The Democratic field is crowded but the midterms have given some likely candidates a boost. Ossoff’s reelection as Georgia Senator has fueled speculation about a 2028 run by a telegenic politician who has already gained attention for mocking Trump’s relationship with a young staffer. The 39-year-old has said that he has “zero interest in running for president” but his swiftly-declared win in Georgia — and his victory speech — have bolstered his status in the party. nigeria.title: ‘I’m PDP member but Wike is not my leader’ — Oyinlola
nigeria.description: Former Osun State Governor, Olagunsoye Oyinlola, has dissociated himself from the Peoples Democratic Party leadership purportedly under the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, saying the minister is not his leader. Oyinlola, a retired general, stated this on Wednesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today programme. When asked whether Wike was his leader in the PDP, the former governor said, “No, not my leader. You don’t say that kind of thing.” He added, “Yes, I am a member of the PDP, but he’s not my leader.” Oyinlola also suggested that Wike was young enough to be his political subordinate, citing their different stages of life when he served as military governor of Lagos State between 1993 and 1996. Asked whether Wike was his boy, he said, “He qualifies to be. When I was governor in Lagos, where was he? In school.” Wike, a PDP member, was appointed FCT minister by President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC). He subsequently established the Rainbow coalition, a political structure backing Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. The coalition has attracted criticism from some PDP members who accuse Wike of working against the party’s interests by supporting the president. Oyinlola, who governed Osun from 2003 to 2010, also blamed the crisis rocking the opposition party on internal forces working against efforts to restore its unity. Speaking about former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s efforts to rebuild the party, Oyinlola said the former president had been working to re-engineer its structure, but some members were frustrating the process. “He’s been trying to ensure that the party is re-engineered. But those who don’t want it are working against it within the party. That’s the much I can say,” he said. Oyinlola maintained that the PDP remained capable of recovering from its internal crisis, noting that it had structures across the country. “The PDP is not dead. The bone will rise again,” he said. He added that the party had a presence in all 774 local government areas and could regain its strength if members resolved their differences. “If we get our acts together, it’s a thing we can achieve, but the forces making sure we don’t get there are there. They are not sleeping,” Oyinlola said. The post ‘I’m PDP member but Wike is not my leader’ — Oyinlola appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Canada unveils budget to curb reliance on US
nigeria.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government presents its budget on Thursday, a plan designed to reduce US reliance, which remains Ottawa’s priority despite President Donald Trump’s midterm election setback. Carney has argued that relations between Canada and the United States have been permanently altered and that pre-Trump tariff-free relations will not return. Carney says Canada needs to urgently diversify its trade relationships and has named Thursday’s budget — his second since taking office last year — “Masters of our Destiny.” “At its core, our plan is about changing Canada’s growth model,” Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne said this week. Champagne, who will present the budget to parliament, added that the goals include boosting domestic commerce within Canada and “diversifying our trade.” “No matter what happens south of the border, no matter what happens in the world, we will be more resilient, we will be stronger, we will be more independent,” Champagne said Wednesday, after selecting a new pair of shoes for his budget speech, keeping a quirky Canadian tradition. Trump’s tariffs have battered Canada’s economy but the future of his protectionist trade measures faced fresh uncertainty after his Republican Party suffered a crushing midterm defeat. Democrats, who have been critical of tariffs on Canada, will take control of both the US House and Senate next year. Senior Democratic Congressman Jamie Raskin told Canada’s public broadcaster CBC on Wednesday that his party is “going to put an end to these tariffs” and will be seeking to repair ties “with our best friends like Canada.” But Canada’s minister responsible for US trade, Dominic LeBlanc, noted Wednesday that negotiations on tariffs will be held with Trump’s White House, not Congress. Canada’s focus, including in the budget, will be on “diversifying our trading relationships,” LeBlanc said. Both Trump and Carney have in recent days sounded optimistic about the prospects of a trade deal, but there were similarly rosy predictions in August before talks broke down. – Major projects – The budget is expected to allocate funds towards the major national projects Carney has tagged as crucial to Canadian economic sovereignty, including infrastructure for energy production and critical mineral mining. Champagne said there will also be support for workers hurt by Trump’s tariffs in sectors like autos and steel. The opposition is likely to raise alarm about deficit spending, but the deficit is expected to be lower than the CAN$78.3 billion ($56.3 billion) projected in Carney’s first budget last year. University of Ottawa political scientist Genevieve Tellier noted that implementation of the budget will in part depend on “the impact of tariffs,” particularly whether Trump’s levies cause further job losses. nigeria.title: FG lists 5 digital banks Nigerians can use to access N50,000 monthly cash support
nigeria.description: The Federal Government has listed five digital banks and mobile money platforms through which selected Nigerians can receive its N50,000 cash support under the National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention (NERSI). According to information published on the NERSI website, beneficiaries can access their funds through ALAT by Wema Bank, MoMo PSB, NairaGram, OPay and Moniepoint. The platforms provide USSD codes and mobile application options for beneficiaries to access their wallets and withdraw or spend the money. The government said beneficiaries would receive an SMS from their designated payment provider with instructions once their wallets had been credited. The five platforms and their access codes are: ALAT (Wema Bank): Dial 945 23#. MoMo (MoMo PSB): Dial 671 0#. NairaGram (Mobile wallet): Dial 726 00#. OPay (Mobile money): Dial 955 20# or use the OPay application. Moniepoint (Microfinance bank): Dial 5573 27# or use the Moniepoint application. How to receive the N50,000 support The NERSI website explained that the cash transfer is designed for poor and vulnerable Nigerian households, with beneficiaries selected through verified national identity records and the National Social Register. According to the programme’s guidelines, selected beneficiaries will receive an SMS from one of the five approved payment providers informing them of their selection. Recipients are required to reply YES to the message to give their consent to participate in the programme. Following confirmation, a mobile wallet linked to the beneficiary’s phone number and National Identification Number (NIN) will be opened, after which the N50,000 support will be credited. Beneficiaries can withdraw the money through a point-of-sale (POS) agent or at a bank, or spend directly from their mobile wallets. FG warns Nigerians against fraud The Federal Government stressed that participation in the programme is free and that beneficiaries are not required to pay any fee, register separately or visit government offices to secure the support. The NERSI website warned Nigerians against fraudsters demanding money to facilitate selection or release of the funds. It also advised beneficiaries not to disclose their personal identification numbers (PINs), one-time passwords (OTPs) or passwords to anyone, including agents and government officials. According to the programme’s guidelines, genuine messages will only come from ALAT, MoMo, NairaGram, OPay or Moniepoint and will only require beneficiaries to reply YES or dial their payment provider’s designated USSD code. The government further stated that not all eligible households would be included in the first batch of beneficiaries, adding that nobody could pay to secure a place on the list. nigeria.title: 2027: Show how many people you killed to prove rigging – Keyamo tells opposition
nigeria.description: Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, has sarcastically challenged opposition politicians to show the number of people they killed during elections to substantiate claims of electoral rigging. Keyamo stated this in a post on his X platform on Thursday while reacting to the emerging slogan, “rig and die”, ahead of the 2027 general elections. He said the phrase should be embraced because it would make it difficult for opposition politicians to blame electoral defeats on rigging after losing elections conducted freely and fairly. On a sarcastic note, the minister argued that those who allege rigging should be asked to account for the number of people killed during the election, suggesting that such deaths should correspond with the scale of alleged electoral manipulation. “The new buzz phrase ‘rig and die’ should excite all of us and we should all embrace it,” he wrote. “The simple reason is that when those who are now trumpeting it lose woefully in a free and fair context, it will be impossible for them to hide their humiliation at the polls under the guise of ‘rigging’ as they have always done. “This is because we will ask them how many ‘riggers’ they killed on the election day, because the number of those killed by them should be directly proportional to the amount of ‘rigging’ that took place!” He added: “In other words, they need to show how many people they killed to prove the election was rigged!! Chai!!” Keyamo’s comments come amid political posturing and exchanges among parties and their supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections. nigeria.title: NMDPRA, EFCC Seal Chinese-Linked Illegal Refinery With 90,000-Litre Underground Tank In Ogun
nigeria.description: The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA), alongside operatives of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), have visited the just-discovered illegal refinery situated in Ogere-Remo, Ikenne Local Government Area of Ogun State, southwest Nigeria. The joint inspection of the place allegedly followed a whistleblowing and intelligence that exposed what investigators described as a well-fenced, crude but technically sophisticated refinery occupying over three hectares of land in the area The inspection team discovered underground tanks believed to have been used for heating and processing sludge oil, waste products from refining, and substances suspected to be Automotive Gas Oil, AGO, otherwise known as diesel. The facility has, however, been sealed on inspection by NMDPRA officials. Speaking during the inspection, the Ogun State Coordinator of NMDPRA, Dr Atilola Akinyemi, said the facility was a complete illegality with no permit from any regulatory authority. He confirmed that the underground storage facility behind the site has an estimated capacity of more than 90,000 litres, with underground heating systems, hydrants for cooling, locally fabricated tanks and silos for separation. “This facility you see here is very crude and completely illegal. This is not a refinery by any standard. It does not have a permit from any regulatory authority, and its operations are unknown to the relevant authorities,” he said. “They appear to be technically skilled people who have deliberately designed this facility to circumvent government regulations. When we examine their final product, it may look like diesel to the average person, but we cannot classify it as diesel until laboratory tests have been conducted,” he warned. Akinyemi maintained that if such adulterated products find their way into the market, vehicles and engines would be exposed to serious risks, adding that all products recovered have now been confiscated by the Federal Government. The EFCC Zonal Director, Lagos Zonal Directorate 2, Bawa Usman Kaltungo, who led the operation, disclosed that the illegal refinery was discovered through whistleblowing. “What we have seen here is an illegal refinery with a complete setup, featuring all the processes through which sludge passes before being converted into what is commonly referred to as diesel. Judging by the nature of this facility, it has been operating for years,” Kalango said. Kalango said the same Ogere axis has become a hub of illegal activities by foreign nationals, recalling that 14 Chinese nationals were arrested a week earlier over illegal lithium processing. “Some of them had passports, while others did not. nigeria.title: Full list: Champions League top scorers after Matchday 4
nigeria.description: Como forward Tasos Douvikas has emerged as the top scorer in the 2026/27 UEFA Champions League following the conclusion of Matchday 4 fixtures. The Greek striker moved to the top of the scoring chart after scoring a hat-trick in Como’s emphatic 9-1 victory over Lens on Wednesday. Douvikas has now scored six goals in four appearances in the competition, finding the net in each of Como’s four league-phase matches. Manchester City striker Erling Haaland and Club Brugge forward Nicolò Tresoldi are joint-second with five goals apiece. Haaland scored the winning goal in Manchester City’s 3-2 victory over RB Leipzig, while Tresoldi was also on target as Club Brugge defeated PSV Eindhoven 2-1. A further 12 players are tied on four goals, including Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane, Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé, Barcelona’s Raphinha, Paris Saint-Germain’s Fabián Ruiz and Borussia Dortmund’s Serhou Guirassy. Raphinha scored twice in Barcelona’s 3-0 win over Aston Villa, while Ruiz also recorded a brace as PSG thrashed Villarreal 6-0. Meanwhile, Real Madrid’s Mbappé was among the goalscorers in his side’s 3-2 victory over AEK Athens. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine American Bitcoin (ABTC) Posts $126 Million Profit as Holdings Gain $197 Million American Bitcoin Corp. (Nasdaq: ABTC) reported about $126 million in third-quarter net income on Wednesday, a swing from a $57.2 million loss in the prior quarter that rested largely on a $197.3 million gain on the company’s bitcoin holdings rather than on mining revenue. The Miami-based miner and treasury company, a majority-owned subsidiary of Hut 8 Corp. and co-founded with Trump family backing, mined about 891 bitcoin in the quarter at a cost of roughly $42,100 each and ended September with about 8,427 BTC. Mining revenue was about $63.4 million, down from about $67.0 million in the second quarter. Gross profit was about $25.8 million, a 41% margin, compared with about $33.0 million and 49% a quarter earlier, as seasonal power costs rose across its sites. Adjusted EBITDA came in at about $221 million, compared with an Adjusted EBITDA loss of about $45.0 million in the second quarter, according to the company’s release . Eric Trump, co-founder and chief strategy officer of American Bitcoin, said the quarter delivered the net income and Adjusted EBITDA figures while growing the bitcoin reserve and bitcoin per share. Chief Executive Mike Ho said the company kept mining at a structural discount to spot and raised satoshis per share by about 5% without issuing shares through its at-the-market program or buying bitcoin on the open market. A paper gain carried American Bitcoin’s quarter The income statement makes the driver plain. American Bitcoin booked a $197.3 million gain on digital assets in the third quarter, after a $71.2 million loss on that line in the second. Operating income was about $191.8 million. Other expense included a $64.3 million loss on derivatives. Strip the mark-to-market move out of the picture and the operating story looks quieter. Revenue per bitcoin mined was about $71,100, down slightly from about $71,900 in the second quarter, and the cost to mine rose to about $42,100 from about $36,500, the company said. Production of about 891 bitcoin was below the second quarter’s roughly 932 coins, which the company had called its highest quarterly haul on record when it reported a $57.2 million second-quarter loss alongside a climb in holdings to about 8,002 BTC. American Bitcoin said it sold a portion of production to cover operating costs while still adding to its strategic reserve. Holdings rose by about 425 bitcoin, or about 5%, to roughly 8,427 as of Sept. 30. That total includes about 3,090 bitcoin pledged for miner purchases under agreements with Bitmain. business.title: Judge Lets Stock Perpetual Futures Keep Trading but Says CFTC Likely Overstepped Its Authority
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Judge Lets Stock Perpetual Futures Keep Trading but Says CFTC Likely Overstepped Its Authority Stock perpetual futures can keep trading on Kalshi, Coinbase Derivatives and Bitnomial for now after a federal judge denied an emergency bid to halt them Tuesday, while finding that the Wall Street-backed challengers are likely to prove the CFTC overstepped its authority. U.S. District Judge Valerie Caproni denied the temporary restraining order on Nov. 3 after a teleconference with the parties, hours after the CFTC said the products could begin trading on U.S.-regulated exchanges. The plaintiff is the Capital Markets Alliance Association, a New York nonprofit whose members include Cboe Global Markets, Citadel Securities and the Healthy Markets Association, according to a declaration from its secretary, Adam Ford. The group sued the CFTC and Chairman Michael S. Selig in the Southern District of New York, case No. 1:26-cv-09608, seeking to undo the approvals of filings by all three exchanges. Caproni wrote that the group “is likely to succeed on the merits” of its claim that the agency lacks statutory authority to allow perpetual derivatives on individual stocks to be offered to retail investors on CFTC-regulated platforms. “Because the perpetual contracts, by definition, do not provide for a ‘sale for future delivery of a single security,’ they cannot be a security future over which the CFTC has statutory and regulatory authority,” she wrote. Instead, she said, the contracts “appear to satisfy the definition of a swap,” which falls to the Securities and Exchange Commission. She also found that the balance of equities and the public interest favor the alliance, writing that the agency’s actions “seem to represent a major disruption to the equities market.” The request failed on one prong. Caproni said the declarations from Cboe, Citadel Securities and Healthy Markets were “conjectural” about the harm members would suffer and did not show irreparable harm that was “actual and imminent.” What the ruling does and does not do The order leaves the approvals in place. It does not decide the case or the alliance’s separate motion for a preliminary injunction. The CFTC’s opposition is due Friday, Nov. 6, and the alliance’s reply is due Tuesday, Nov. 10. The order says that schedule is subject to change by the assigned judge. The docket lists Judge Lorna G. Schofield as assigned to the case. Kalshi was already listing four single-stock perps on Qualcomm, McDonald’s, Amgen and Costco by Wednesday morning, with maximum leverage of 4.9 times. Bloomberg Law reported that the judge signaled she might ultimately side with the Wall Street firms opposed to the products. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. sports.title: Former F1 champion Jones dies aged 80
sports.description: Jones helped turn Williams into one of the major forces in F1 [Getty Images] Alan Jones, the last Australian and first Williams driver to win the Formula 1 world title, has died at the age of 80. Jones raced in F1 between 1975 and 1986, winning the title in 1980 to become the first of Williams' seven world champions. Jones, who turned 80 on Monday, won 12 grands prix in his career and raced competitively in other formats until 2002. "We are extremely saddened to announce the passing of our beloved Alan, who passed away on 5 November following a short illness," his wife Amanda Butler-Davis said in a statement released on her behalf by Motorsport Australia. "He will be dearly missed and fondly remembered by those closest to him, as well as the many fans whose support he was always grateful for." Jones started the first of his 116 F1 races in a Hesketh at the 1975 Spanish Grand Prix. He won his first race for the Shadow team in Austria in 1977 before joining Williams the following year. After finishing third in the drivers' championship in 1979, he won five races in 1980 and finished on the podium in all but one of the grands prix he completed, taking the title ahead of Nelson Piquet. Jones was the second Australian to win the F1 championship, after Jack Brabham in 1959, 1960 and 1966. Jones remains the most recent Australian to triumph at the Australian Grand Prix, winning at Melbourne's Calder Park Raceway in 1980 when the race was not part of the world championship. He finished third in the drivers' standings in 1981, winning in Las Vegas for what proved to be his final race victory. He retired at the end of the season. Having appeared in one race for Arrows in 1983, Jones made a full-time comeback with new team Haas in 1985 and raced largely unsuccessfully the following year. He continued to compete in touring car and endurance races, mostly in Australia, and became a popular motorsports pundit on television in his home country. "Alan dedicated his life to motorsport, building a legacy that will live on through the countless people he touched along the way," Butler-Davis said. "Through his achievements, passion and unmistakable character, both on and off the track, Alan left an enduring mark on the sport both nationally and across the globe." Breaking new ground with Williams Jones, the Williams FW07 and Patrick Head and Frank Williams in Brazil in 1981 [Getty Images] Alan Jones' time at the very peak of F1 was short - essentially just under three years from mid-1979 to the end of 1981 - but he left a lasting impression. Jones is synonymous with the Williams team, having become their first world champion in 1980, and he formed a close, almost brotherly bond with co-founders Frank Williams and Patrick Head. Williams and Head loved Jones' pugnacious, no-nonsense approach, and between them they were the leading force in F1 for a short time, as the team first emerged at the forefront of the sport. sports.title: One year after 'Let it Rip' meeting, Trevor Lawrence has elevated game
sports.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars were a surprising 4-3, but his quarterback was still searching to sync his in-week preparation and game-day production when Liam Coen welcomed Trevor Lawrence into his second-floor office on Oct. 20, 2025. Lawrence was a tireless worker who made the right pre-snap decisions but was plagued by bouts of indecisiveness. Before sending him on his bye week, Coen showed Lawrence multiple examples in which the play was right there had he pulled the trigger. “I just have to trust it,” Lawrence told Coen. The summit could eventually be remembered as one of the most important meetings — The "Let It Rip" meeting — in Jaguars history. The coach showed confidence and belief in his franchise quarterback but also urged him to be more aggressive. In the 17 regular season games since, the Jaguars are 14-3 and Lawrence has totals of 37 touchdowns, 11 interceptions, 4,669 passing yards, a 63.9 completion rate and a 109.9 passer rating. High-level stuff. MVP stuff. Winning stuff. A player who used to tease with bits of elite play is now one of the NFL’s best quarterbacks. He enters the Jaguars’ Nov. 5 game at the Baltimore Ravens with a league-best 112.6 passer rating; he started the season with a career 86.3 rating. The Jaguars are 5-2 thanks in part to Lawrence’s level-jump — check that, multi-level jump. Just as the Chicago Bears have been reborn with the Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams, so have the Jaguars with Coen and Lawrence. Admit it: For the first time since maybe 1999, you, the Jaguars fan, expects your team to win every week and when they don’t, there is a sky-is-falling reaction. Feels good, doesn’t it? It sure does within Jaguars headquarters, where the collaboration between Coen and Lawrence has advanced to the pro football equivalent of Ph.D. courses. “Very far,” Coen told The Times-Union on Oct. 20 of Lawrence's progress. “I’m very, very pleased with how he’s seeing things.” What is it like to be around Coen and Lawrence in the quarterback meeting room, when class is in session and plays are tossed out, added or revised? Over the last two weeks, the Times-Union tried to find out. Coen-Lawrence talks have ‘evolved’ So, you’re Joey Aguilar , an undrafted rookie who two years ago was playing at Appalachian State or you’re Quinn Ewers , a second-year player who two years ago was playing at Texas and was traded to the Jaguars on Aug. 29. sports.title: Jeremiah Smith is 164 yards from another Big Ten record
sports.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 31: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes in action against the USC Trojans during the second quarter at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on October 31, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images Lost in the frustration of Ohio State’s 30-18 loss at USC was another piece of history from Jeremiah Smith. With just over two minutes left, Luke Fahey found him for a one yard touchdown. It was the 40th touchdown catch of Smith’s career, breaking Braylon Edwards’ Big Ten record of 39, which had stood since 2004. It didn’t feel like much of a celebration in the moment, but it’s worth remembering just how fast Smith is rewriting the record books. Smith already owns every major receiving record at Ohio State, and now he holds the Big Ten’s career touchdown mark too. The next record could fall this Saturday. The yardage record is within reach Smith caught 10 passes for 83 yards at USC, giving him 3,625 career receiving yards. The Big Ten record belongs to Purdue’s John Standeford, who finished with 3,788 yards from 2000 to 2003. That puts Smith 163 yards from tying the record and 164 from breaking it. That’s a big number for most receivers. For Smith, it’s an ordinary afternoon. He had 151 yards against Ball State, 164 at Texas, 217 against Illinois and 206 at Iowa. He’s averaging over 130 receiving yards per game this season, with 62 catches for 1,067 yards and 13 touchdowns through eight games. When I wrote about the Big Ten record chase in early October, I predicted JJ would break this one at USC on Halloween. Sayin’s injury, a quiet day at Indiana and USC’s game plan pushed it back a week. The timing might work out even better. Breaking it at home against Oregon, in front of the Ohio Stadium crowd, would be a pretty fitting way to do it. Can he get there with Fahey? That’s the real question. Smith’s production has dipped over the last two games. Against Indiana, he had a season-low 68 yards against a defense that threw extra bodies at him on almost every snap. At USC, with Fahey making his first start, he caught 10 passes but averaged just 8.3 yards per catch as Ohio State leaned on quick, short throws. That makes sense. Fahey needed easy completions, and Smith is the most reliable target on the field. But it also means the big plays haven’t been there. To get 164 yards against Oregon, Smith will probably need at least one or two explosive plays down the field. I think there’s reason to believe those will come. Fahey now has a full game under his belt and another week of practice as the starter. Smith said after Indiana that it would, “take time” to build the same chemistry with a new quarterback, but he’s already Fahey’s top target. Smith also caught the record breaking touchdown at USC, which tells you Fahey is looking for him when it matters most. The more reps those two get together, the more comfortable Fahey should be giving Smith a chance to make a play down the field.

sports.title: Marco Rose embraces Premier League life and jokes about Thomas Tuchel
sports.description: Marco Rose embraces Premier League life and jokes about Thomas Tuchel Former Bundesliga coach Marco Rose has spoken enthusiastically about his first months in English football. The 50-year-old, who previously coached Borussia Mönchengladbach, Borussia Dortmund, and RB Leipzig, is currently enjoying an upturn in fortunes with AFC Bournemouth following a difficult start to the Premier League campaign. After failing to win any of their opening six league fixtures, Bournemouth have recently registered three consecutive victories. Rose’s side have also enjoyed success in European competition, with the German trainer preparing for Thursday’s Europa League encounter against Sparta Prague. Speaking in an interview with Kicker , Rose reflected on his experience in the Premier League and the differences between German and English football. “It’s something special to be able to work there,” Rose explained. “One senses the global attention. It’s football in its purest form. I appreciate German fan culture, but I also like the English version. It’s a little quieter here at times, but when the match calls for it, the stadiums generate extraordinary energy. I like the people in England, who treat one another with great respect. I really feel comfortable here.” Marco Rose jokes about Thomas Tuchel and Marcus Tavernier Rose also reserved praise for Bournemouth attacker Marcus Tavernier, who has scored five goals in nine Premier League appearances this season. Asked whether the 26-year-old might soon receive a call-up from England national team coach Thomas Tuchel, Rose declined to speculate but acknowledged his player’s impressive performances. “You’ll have to ask Thomas about that,” Rose remarked. “But I think several of our lads have made a good case for themselves, and Marcus in particular gives us a great deal.” When asked whether Tuchel had attended a Bournemouth home fixture to watch Tavernier, Rose delivered a lighthearted response. “No, I don’t think so,” Rose said with a laugh. “Perhaps he couldn’t get a ticket because our stadium is a little smaller.” GGFN | Peter Weis

Now, they must assess themselves as they prepare for the future. Here are three questions they must ask if they want to continue their prolonged success into 2027 and beyond. In the Market for Pitching Again? Los Angeles knows better than most that one can never have enough pitching. To that end, they traded for Tarik Skubal at the trade deadline this year. Now, are they willing to keep him? The left-hander is expected to earn a pretty penny this year. Moreover, he has Scott Boras as his agent and an abbreviated window with which to negotiate as December 1 approaches. Los Angeles and President of Baseball Operations Andrew Friedman have plenty of money at their disposal, provided that their owner doesn’t sell the team. Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) pitches during the first inning of their National League Championship Series game against the Milwaukee Brewers at American Family Field on Oct 11, 2026. However, Los Angeles, with a few notable exceptions, is very hesitant to dole out long-term contracts to a player entering free agency who is entering his third decade. The more likely option for a mutual agreement would be a shorter deal in length with a higher AAV, similar to the Kyle Tucker deal. It is said that Los Angeles has some competition for the left-hander’s services; the New York Mets and Chicago Cubs are also interested. Skubal did seem to like it in Los Angeles, but it’s still a question where he will end up. However, those in the know expect a deal signed by December 1. The Youth Movement? Los Angeles has the oldest roster in baseball, and it showed during the National League Championship Series against the World Champion Milwaukee Brewers. The question is how young will the Dodgers go without compromising the veteran core? There is no question that there will be some turnover on the margins. Enrique and Teoscar Hernandez will probably be on different teams in 2027. Josue DePaula will probably cement his place on the roster. Do they sign or trade for a shortstop like Elly de La Cruz ? Will they move Mookie Betts to second base to preserve him from wear and tear on his body? Friedman, in his year-end press conference, addressed the age of the players, but he didn’t seem overly concerned right now. sports.description: Jul 31, 2018; San Diego, CA, USA; San Diego Padres catcher A.J. Ellis looks on during the tenth inning against the San Francisco Giants at Petco Park. Mandatory Credit: Orlando Ramirez-USA TODAY Sports | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor The New York Mets are hiring A.J. Ellis as their major-league strategy coordinator, The Athletic’s Will Sammon reported Wednesday. The club has not yet announced the move. Ellis becomes the latest addition to manager Andy Green’s coaching staff as the Mets continue preparing for the 2027 season. His arrival also reunites Green with a familiar face from his time managing the San Diego Padres. Mets Hiring A.J. Ellis to Major-League Coaching Staff Ellis, 45, played 11 major-league seasons, most notably with the Los Angeles Dodgers. He also spent time with the Philadelphia Phillies and Miami Marlins before finishing his playing career with San Diego in 2018. Across 672 career games, Ellis hit .239 with 44 home runs and 229 RBI. While his offensive numbers were modest, his experience behind the plate gave him years of working closely with pitchers and handling major-league pitching staffs. Following his retirement, Ellis joined the Padres’ front office as a special assistant in 2019. He now brings both playing and front-office experience to his new role in New York. During his final season as a player, Ellis played under Green in San Diego. That existing relationship could help ease his transition to the Mets, giving him familiarity with the manager as he joins a different organization. Ellis also gained experience mentoring younger players late in his career, helping Padres catchers Austin Hedges and Francisco Mejía in 2018. That background could prove valuable as he establishes relationships with players in New York. The Last Word With one coaching vacancy remaining — after this move becomes official and the promotion of Mariano Duncan — the staff is moving closer to completion. Ellis’ addition gives Green another experienced voice as the Mets look to turn their offseason preparations into better results in 2027. Vasquez-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor The Major League Baseball deadline to extend qualifying offers to players was Monday, November 2, at 5 p.m. A qualifying offer is a one-year offer extended by a team to a player who spent the entire previous year with the team-a player can only receive a qualifying offer once. The Yankees had two qualifying offer-eligible players: David Bednar and Jazz Chisholm Jr. While the Yankees extended an offer to Bednar worth $23.15 million, they did not extend one to Chisholm Jr. Why exactly is that, and where do the Yankees go at second base? Where do the Yankees Turn to at Second Base? For starters, Bednar is one of the best closers in baseball. He recorded the third most saves in the American League with 35 this season while posting a 2.47 ERA. After getting traded to the Yankees from Pittsburgh at the 2025 trade deadline, he’s gone 45/52 in save opportunities. He was well deserving of his qualifying offer. Chisholm Jr., on the other hand, had a down season by his standards. He had the worst batting average for a full season at .231 with 19 home runs, a below-league-average OPS at .711 and a 1.7 WAR. However, more positively, he recorded 15 outs above average and stole 41 bases. sports.title: Frank Bruno names the biggest puncher he ever faced
sports.description: When you talk to any boxing fan, especially a British boxing fan, they will likely have plenty of positives to say about former WBC heavyweight champion Frank Bruno. The London-born fighter was beloved by the British public and considered a man of the people. He faced some of the best fighters of his generation, and when appearing on the Fight Your Corner podcast with Tony Bellew and Charlie Parsons , Bruno revealed the five biggest punchers he faced, including who hit harder than Mike Tyson . Frank Bruno ranks five biggest punchers he faced When asked on the Fight Your Corner podcast to rank the five biggest punchers he’s faced, Frank Bruno said: “Bone Crusher Smith was a hard puncher. I would say Tim Witherspoon (hardest puncher).” “He was a dangerous puncher. Very slick, knows his business,” added Bruno. When asked if James “Bone Crusher” Smith was second, Bruno said: “Yeah, definitely.” Revealing the third-biggest puncher, the former WBC champ said: “Mike Tyson at his peak.” Bellew asked Bruno if Tyson was the most ruthless, and he said: “Most definitely, when he’s on his game.” Discussing who would be fourth and fifth out of Oliver McCall and Lennox Lewis: “Oliver McCall. He’s mad. Something’s not right. Very strong guy,” said the Brit. Those selections left Lewis in position five, revealing the five biggest punchers that Bruno ever faced. Frank Bruno Personal Instagram @frankbrunoboxer The Big Fight Weekend verdict Growing up in the era when Frank Bruno (40-5, 38 KOs) was fighting, he was loved by the British public; there is no doubt. My Mum actually met Frank Bruno once and described him as a gentleman after they met at Notting Hill Market back in the 90s. Outside the ring, he was a gentle giant with fans he met. Inside the ring, he mixed with the best, losing twice to Mike Tyson and once to Tim Witherspoon, Lennox Lewis, and James “Bone Crusher Smith.” He memorably went through the trenches to outpoint Oliver McCall to win the WBC title by unanimous decision, with scorecards 115-113 and 117-111 x2. Bruno has gone through his own mental health battles since retiring, but he remains a loved cultural figure in the UK. He may not have been the greatest technical fighter, but he was the most loved. Photograph: Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images Before a single vote was cast this election cycle, the technocrats and oligarchs who own American sports had already voted. Pro sports owners put more than $100m into this cycle, according to Front Office Sports. But Tuesday night was a referendum not just on Donald Trump and Maga policies, but on the puppeteers who pull America’s strings. The people voted, and the owners lost. Before anyone frames this as a rescue, a word about the rescuers. Democrats are the instrument for ending Maga, and they are also the other face of the same coin. Think Republicans are behind all of our ills? Think again. New Jersey’s governor, Phil Murphy, placed his state’s first legal sports bet in 2018. Illinois governor JB Pritzker signed sports betting into law a year later. New York’s mobile sportsbooks went live under Governor Kathy Hochul in 2022, with the state taking 51% of the revenue. Pritzker and Hochul both won Tuesday, and all of them are Democrats. In some of the biggest betting markets in the country, the bookmakers’ most reliable partner has been a Democratic statehouse. Having said all that, the biggest losers on Tuesday night were Republicans: Democrats flipped both chambers of Congress. That would have made plenty of sports owners disappointed, as they have a habit of backing Republicans. At least 10 sports owners backed Mike Rogers in Michigan, and Abdul El-Sayed beat Rogers . Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones gave $1m to Trump’s super Pac and $250,000 to a committee backing Ken Paxton, and James Talarico beat Paxton in Texas. The former Mavericks owner Miriam Adelson lapped everyone with at least $67m to Republican committees, in keeping with her history of big spending around elections. What did she get for her money? A House and Senate minority. So how does all this affect the future of American sports? Let’s count the ways. The league’s brief makes two arguments: prediction markets are gambling that belongs under state regulation like any sportsbook, and the money is enormous. Football drew $1.8bn in prediction-market trades on the season’s opening Sunday, more than half of everything traded. technology.title: Royal London plans IT outsourcing shake-up as staff brace for redundancies
technology.description: Royal London plans to cut hundreds of IT jobs and shift work to India under an outsourcing deal with IBM, according to sources, with redundancies expected by the end of December. Sources said Royal London's chief technology officer, James Sandell, told IT staff in September that the insurance and pensions giant was partnering with IBM to outsource a substantial portion of its technology operations. A consultation process was expected to follow. A Royal London spokesperson told The Register : "Royal London has appointed IBM as its strategic technology infrastructure partner as it continues to develop its technology strategy. The partnership will give Royal London access to IBM’s specialist capability, scale and experience. Royal London will remain accountable for service delivery and regulatory requirements and continues to focus on ensuring continuity and quality of service for customers." We asked Royal London how many UK IT roles it would retain and whether IBM would move work to India. The exact number of jobs at risk remains unclear, although one Glassdoor review posted on October 6 claims that hundreds of positions in the company's technology operations division are being eliminated. "A vast amount of knowledge is being lost by the business, a lot that is not yet documented due to constant years of recruitment freeze and workload volume," they wrote. The reviewer also questioned whether management had grasped just how much work would be involved in handing operations over to IBM, particularly with already stretched teams being cut to a fraction of their former size. Royal London replied to the Glassdoor review, acknowledging staff concerns about the changes, though it didn't comment on the claims about outsourcing and redundancies. "We recognise that as Royal London is going through a period of transformation, this has raised questions and concerns for some colleagues," the company wrote. "We have established channels for colleagues to raise these, including through People Leaders and Colleague Representatives, and I encourage colleagues to use these routes to discuss their concerns." Other October reviews questioned the handling of the outsourcing and Royal London's commitment to its mutual values. An October 12 reviewer identifying themselves as an IT infrastructure employee said the company had historically offered good career prospects, before criticizing its new direction. "Sudden outsourcing goes against all Royal London values," the reviewer wrote, adding that employees were questioning the company's direction amid reports of a hiring freeze and further potential cuts. Another review, posted on October 20, suggested the IBM deal was the latest in a series of outsourcing decisions following an earlier move to transfer servicing jobs to South Africa. technology.title: When datacenters lose power, generators should kick in. That didn’t happen for Google in London
technology.description: Google Cloud has revealed that the cause of the October 20 outage in its europe-west-2-b availability zone was a ‘misconfiguration’ of its systems that meant its emergency generators didn’t start. The outage at the London facility caused service interruptions at outfits including Lloyds, HSBC, Royal Mail, and Revolut. In a November 4 update to its service status page, Google explained what went wrong. “The site relies on a 2N utility power architecture — where the facility has complete duplicate power paths for every critical load — backed by a central high-voltage generator bank managed by a dual-redundant Programmable Logic Controller (PLC),” Google revealed. The facility gets its juice from two independent utility feeders, which Google calls “A” and “B”. There’s also a “standby utility connection configured for manual campus-wide transfer during maintenance operations or emergency events.” Google says the root cause of the incident was failure in an external underground cable through which its power supplier brings ‘leccy to its bit barns. That cable connects to primary feeder A and it broke at a time when feeder B wasn’t working. “Circuit breaker feeder B was physically opened to allow for corrective repairs following issues identified during a quarterly generator load test on 14 Oct 2026,” Google admitted. “Consequently, primary utility feed A was supporting the total critical load while the feed B breaker remained in an open position to allow repairs to be conducted on the B feeder pathway.” That shouldn’t be a problem for a top-tier operator like Google, which knows it needs to install backup sources of electricity like uninterruptible power supplies (UPS) and on-site generators. Indeed, europe-west-2-b employs UPSes that Google says can keep things up and running for five minutes if the availability zone loses its connection to the grid. The UPSes worked, but a “voltage-sensing design flaw and PLC misconfiguration prevented the facility’s generator plant from receiving an automatic start signal to assume the critical load.” Google’s UPSes therefore ran out of juice, but its generators didn’t start. The rest is history. The search giant has figured out that its PLCs weren’t set up to handle the conditions it faced on this fateful day. “PLC logic indicated that a healthy utility source was available, even though the primary and secondary distribution feeds were de-energized, and did not issue a start command to the generator plant,” the status update reveals. Once Google was able to reconnect to its power utility, it reprogrammed the PLC so it wouldn’t make the same mistake again. The Big G has since made many changes to the electrical setup at europe-west-2-b and says it’s tested them and that they all work. We based our report about vSphere Express on an interview, and on material provided by VMware – which sent a version of the blog post linked to above. The version we saw did not include the following paragraph, the contents of which were not mentioned in our interview: “Furthermore, for customers in countries in the European Economic Area, vSphere Standard version 8 and vSphere Enterprise Plus version 8 will remain available for sale until October 31, 2027, and will have Extended Support included in any active subscriptions to those offerings until the earlier of the applicable subscription end date or October 31, 2028.” The latter date is more than a year past the October 11, 2027, end-of-general-support date for the more capable vSphere 8 and Cloud Foundation 5.x products. “This has the potential to be a positive development for organisations within the European Economic Area,” independent analyst Michael Warrilow told The Register . “It could provide them up to an extra 12 months to transition vSphere 8 to VCF 9 and/or migrate workloads to another platform.” Warrilow thinks European users should seek “absolute clarity” from VMware about the specifics of its offer. “What level of extended support will be provided and what longer-term commitments will need to be made? I cannot find any of that detail,” he wrote. A reminder: VMware has promised in the past to make patches available for users who choose to persist with perpetual licenses instead of moving to its preferred subscriptions. The Broadcom business unit later paused patch downloads for months, claiming it needed to adjust its website to make them possible. Warrilow wonders why VMware will keep selling vSphere Standard only in Europe and suggested “regulatory muscle” is the reason. Regulators around the world cleared Broadcom’s acquisition of VMware.
